name: Land cover legend for Punjab Province, Pakistan

class.name: Built-up
class.definition: The land covered by buildings, roads and artificial surfaced ar-eas. Different types of build-up are included in this class (i.e. urban, airports, oilfields). Non-vegetated areas are character-ized by NDVI values close to zero.

class.name: Roads
class.definition: Linear artificial structures, mainly major roads (motor-ways, primary roads).

class.name: Tree orchards
class.definition: Orchards are areas cultivated for the production of fruits, nuts, and other type of plantations. Areas covered by orchards are characterized by NDVI values very similar to the one shown by tree closed land cover class.

class.name: Herbaceous crops irrigated
class.definition: Agricultural areas characterized by ex-tensive irrigational facilities. The pres-ence channels for irrigation is a distinc-tive factor of this land cover class. The greenness associated with irrigated sites is generally independent of rainfall. Irri-gated crops have 2 higher peaks corre-sponding to the two main crop seasons: Kharif (first sowing season from April – June and harvested during October – December) with the main crops such as rice, sugarcane, cotton and maize and Rabi (second sowing season from Octo-ber – December and harvested in April – May) with main crops such as cereals and oil seeds.

class.name: Herbaceous crops rainfed
class.definition: Rainfed agricul-ture relies only on rainfall for wa-ter, therefore NDVI values strictly depend on rainfall pat-tern over the year but the gen-eral aspect re-flects the two main crop sea-sons.

class.name: Herbaceous crops in flood plain
class.definition: Herbaceous crop located only in proximity of the riverbed is termed as crop in floodplain. The water supply is provided either by irrigation or by the annual floods. Crop in flood-plain includes herbaceous crop irrigated in flood plain and herbaceous crop post-flooding

class.name: Herbaceous natural vegetation
class.definition: Relatively dense herba-ceous natural vegetation, occasionally with sparse shrubs and trees. NDVI values are very low throughout the year

class.name: Shrubs sparse natural vegetation
class.definition: Natural open shrubs, occasionally with sparse or closed herba-ceous vegetation cov-er, with percentage cover varying from 10 to 60%.

class.name: Shrubs dense natural vegetation
class.definition: Natural closed shrubs with shrubs percentage cover of more than 60%. In Punjab the forest cover is limited, and it is pre-dominantly scrub forest

class.name: Shrubs in temporary wet soil
class.definition: This class includes areas mainly covered by shrubs of-ten with herbaceous vegeta-tion, usually flooded or liable to flooding by fresh, stagnant or circulating water.

class.name: Trees sparse natural vegetation
class.definition: Natural open trees, occasionally with sparse or closed her-baceous vegetation cover, with percent-age cover varying from 10 to 60%.

class.name: Tree forest plantations
class.definition: Tree forest plantation refers to governmental plantation. This class can be identified with large area and regular shape.

class.name: Trees dense natural vegetation
class.definition: Natural closed trees with tree percentage cover of more than 60%. In Punjab the forest cover is limited, and it is predomi-nantly scrub forest. The co-niferous forests are mainly present in the northern mountainous areas.

class.name: Sand dunes
class.definition: Bare area/undifferentiated area not used for cultivation and usually devoid of grass and shrub cover. Non-vegetated areas are charac-terized by NDVI values close to zero.

class.name: Bare soil
class.definition: Bare area/undifferentiated area not used for cultivation and usually devoid of grass and shrub cover. Non-vegetated ar-eas are characterized by NDVI values close to zero.

class.name: Bare soil in temporary wet
class.definition: Part of the river bed flooded during the rainy season (flood plain).

class.name: Water bodies
class.definition: Natural and artificial non-perennial fresh water body (flowing and standing).

class.name: Wetlands
class.definition: Wetlands are herbaceous vege-tation with cover ranging from 60% to 100% found in flood-ed/wet areas, sometimes asso-ciated with shrubs. NDVI values are higher during the summer season when the progressive reduction of water surface leaves space to the natural vegetation growth.

name: National land cover legend for Bangladesh

class.name: Evergreen hill forest
class.definition: Natural forest area within the reserve forest boundary and protected forest boundary of Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) is known as hill forest. It consists of moist tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen trees. Tree cover ranges from 80% - 100% and top canopy of trees reach a height of 25-62 m.

class.name: Forest plantation
class.definition: The area where trees are planted for high volume of timber and wood under long-term or short- term management. Trees are generally even- aged, planted in rows in a large enough area. Tree height ranges 5 – 40 m and cover ranges 80% - 100%. Agroforestry can also be incorporated with this class.

class.name: Swamp forest
class.definition: Land dominated by evergreen trees which are inundated with freshwater seasonally. Trees grows to about 15–25 m in height with a large canopy. Root of these trees are in two level. One in the ground, and another in the mid-level which is used while the forest is flooded in the monsoon time. Main species are Koroch and Hizal tree

class.name: Rubber plantation
class.definition: The large area where rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) is planted for latex production. Trees are planted in well-drained soil with 3%-32% slope. It is broadleaved, deciduous in the drier month for a very short period. It grows 30 – 40 m and cover ranging from 80% – 100%.

class.name: Mangrove forest
class.definition: The geographical area dominated by halophytic trees with a canopy cover of 85% to 100% and tree height vary from 5m - 17m. The forest floor inundated twice daily by brackish water. The forest is intersected by numerous rivers and creeks.

class.name: Plain land forest (sal forest)
class.definition: Land dominated with tropical moist deciduous forests are known as plain land sal forest. The main species is Sal (Shorea robusta) and its occurrence is 80% - 100% within the patches. Tree height is 5 -25 m and it covers ranging from 60% - 100%.

class.name: Orchards & other plantations (trees)
class.definition: Land dominated with tree species for harvesting fruits. In general, trees are even-aged, planted and managed in rows and cover a large enough area. Marginal land plantations (road, railway, embankment, and canal side) are also included in this class.

class.name: Mangrove plantation
class.definition: Mangrove plantations on newly accreted land in the estuaries of the Bay of Bengal to provide protection against natural calamities and land erosion.

class.name: Bamboo forest
class.definition: Bamboo forest is woody grass of more than 4 m and its occurrence is more than 80% within the patches. It naturally occurs and it covers ranging from 80% - 100%. It is perennial evergreen and it grows up to 15 m. The bamboo resources in the villages areas not included in this class.

class.name: Orchards & other plantations (shrubs)
class.definition: Land dominated by shrubs which are cultivated and managed for fruits and leaf harvesting. This class mainly includes tea gardens. The use of shade trees in tea cultivation is a vital and integral component.

class.name: Rivers/khals
class.definition: Natural water courses serving as water drainage channels.

class.name: Single crop
class.definition: This class includes permanent agriculture lands cultivated with a single herbaceous crop in a year and the same herbaceous crop is cultivated in the same land for several years. Fields may be flooded in monsoon but not in the growing season.

class.name: Herb dominated area
class.definition: The geographic area which is dominated by grass with very little to no woody vegetation is called herb dominated area. These types of vegetation are generally found in newly accreted land, year round fallow land or adjacent to the international boundary of Bangladesh. The coverage is 20 - 100%.

class.name: Multiple crop
class.definition: This class includes permanent agriculture lands which are cultivated with more than one herbaceous crop (Two or Three) in different growing season sequentially (crop diversified in time) within a year and the same crop rotation is practiced in the same land for several years.

class.name: Shifting cultivation
class.definition: This class includes lands where herbaceous crops are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned and allowed to return to their natural vegetation while the farmer moves on to another area.

class.name: Baor
class.definition: Baor is a natural water body and a dead section of a river where it has changed its course. It normally is a part of the floodplain of the river to which inlets and outlets connect it.

class.name: Perennial beels/haors
class.definition: Natural water reservoir, billabong or a lake-like wetland with static water. It becomes very extensive water body in the monsoon and dries up mostly in the post-monsoon period.

class.name: Standing artificial water body - lake
class.definition: Artificial/Natural standing water reservoir that is bigger than a pond. It is an area of variable size filled with water, localized in a basin, that is surrounded by land, apart from any river or other outlet that serves to feed or drain the lake.

class.name: Ponds
class.definition: pond is a human-constructed body of standing water with an area of variable size that is usually smaller than a lake.

class.name: Brackish water aquaculture
class.definition: Large brackish water ponds used for year round brackish water aquaculture.

class.name: Fresh water aquaculture
class.definition: Fresh water ponds used for year round aquaculture.

class.name: Mud flats or inter tidal areas
class.definition: Mud flats or intertidal areas are wet land soil near the estuary. It is submerged and exposed twice daily by tidal water.

class.name: Built-up non-linear
class.definition: This category describes built-up areas where non-linear artificial constructions cover the land with an impervious surface.

class.name: Beach/sand bar
class.definition: Beaches are narrow, gently sloping strip of natural land that lies along the coast and usually consists of loose particles, which are composed of sand. Sand bar are sand deposits within the river channels or in the estuary which are emerging as islands

class.name: Dump sites/ extraction sites
class.definition: Extraction site is defined by the absence of the original natural (semi-natural) cover or water surface and land cover, rock or earthy materials are removed by human activity or machinery.

class.name: River banks
class.definition: The river bank is the natural land alongside the bed of a river which is usually consists of soil and sand deposits and inundated when water course flows with full capacity.

class.name: Air port
class.definition: Built-up areas with facilities for flights to take off and land.

class.name: Salt pans
class.definition: Land used for salt production from seawater by solar evaporation

class.name: Rural settlement
class.definition: Geographic areas of clustered or linear rural dwelling (mainly wooden and tin roof) covered by fruit trees and other plantation and functionally linked with small scale vegetables gardens, open spaces and ponds around the dwellings. Rural markets or growth centers within the rural environment are also included in this class.

class.name: Swap plantation
class.definition: The land dominated by evergreen trees, which are cultivated and inundated in monsoon with freshwater, is known as Swamp Plantation. Trees grows to about 5-45m in height with a large canopy.

class.name: Shrubs with scattered trees
class.definition: This class includes natural woody vegetation of less than 5 m in height. The uppermost canopy layer may be dominated by trees. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.

class.name: Swamp reed land
class.definition: The geographical area which is dominated by reed shrub and the root system is influenced by the fresh water is known as swamp reed land.

class.name: Brickfields
class.definition: Geographic areas used for bricks production

name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Artificial surfaces (including urban and associated areas)
class.definition: The category is composed of any type of artificial surfaces
class.description: The class is composed of any type of areas with a predominant artificial surface. Any urban or related feature is included in this class, for example, urban parks (parks, parkland and laws). The class also includes industrial areas, and waste dump deposit and extraction sites.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Herbaceous crops
class.definition: The category is composed of a main layer of cultivated herbaceous plants.
class.description: The class is composed of a main layer of cultivated herbaceous plants (graminoids or forbs). It includes herbaceous crops used for hay. All the non-perennial crops that do not last for more than two growing seasons and crops like sugar cane, where the upper part of the plant is regularly harvested while the root system can remain for more than one year in the field, are included in this class.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Woody crops
class.definition: The category is composed of a main layer of cultivated tree or shrub plants.
class.description: The class is composed of a main layer of permanent crops (trees or shrub crops) and includes all types of orchards and plantations (fruit trees, coffee and tea plantation, oil palms, rubber plantation, Christmas trees, etc.).
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Multiple or layered crops
class.definition: The category is composed of at least two layers of cultivated woody and herbaceous plants or different layers of cultivated plants combined with natural vegetation.
class.description: This class combine two different land cover situations: 1. Two layers of different crops. A common case is the presence of one layer of woody crops (trees or shrubs) and another layer of herbaceous crop, e.g., wheat fields with olive trees in the Mediterranean area and intense horticulture, or oasis or typical coastal agriculture in Africa, where herbaceous fields are covered by palm trees. 2. Presence of one important layer of natural vegetation (mainly trees) that covers one layer of cultivated crops. Coffee plantations shadowed by natural trees in the equatorial area of Africa are a typical example.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Grassland
class.definition: The category is composed of a main layer of natural herbaceous vegetation with a cover from 10 to 100 per cent.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural herbaceous plants (grasslands, prairies, steppes and savannahs) with a cover of 10 per cent or more, irrespective of different human and/or animal activities, such as grazing or selective fire management. Woody plants (trees and/or shrubs) can be present, assuming their cover is less that 10 per cent.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Trees covered areas
class.definition: The category is composed of a main layer of natural trees with a cover from 10 to 100 per cent.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural tree plants with a cover of 10 per cent or more. Other types of plants (shrubs and/or herbs) can be present, even with a density higher than that of trees. Areas planted with trees for afforestation purposes and forest plantations are included in this class. This class includes areas seasonally or permanently flooded with freshwater. It excludes coastal mangroves (→07).
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Mangroves
class.definition: The category is composed of natural trees with a cover from 10 to 100 per cent in aquatic or regularly flooded areas in salt and brackish water.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by woody vegetation (trees and/or shrubs) with a cover of 10 per cent or more that is permanently or regularly flooded by salt and/or brackish water located in the coastal areas or in the deltas of rivers.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Shrub covered areas
class.definition: The category is composed of a main layer of natural shrubs with a cover from 10 to 100 per cent.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural shrubs having a cover of 10 per cent or more. Trees can be present in scattered form if their cover is less than 10 per cent. Herbaceous plants can also be present at any density. The class includes shrub-covered areas permanently or regularly flooded by inland fresh water. It excludes shrubs flooded by salt or brackish water in coastal areas (→07).
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Shrubs and/or herbaceous vegetation, aquatic or regularly flooded
class.definition: The category is composed of natural shrubs or herbs with a cover from 10 to 100 percent in aquatic or regularly flooded areas with water persistence from 2 to 12 months per year.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural herbaceous vegetation (cover of 10 per cent or more) that is permanently or regularly flooded by fresh or rackish water (swamps, marsh areas, etc.). Flooding must persist for at least two months per year to be considered regular. Woody vegetation (trees and/or shrubs) can be present if their cover is less than 10 per cent.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Sparsely natural vegetated areas
class.definition: The category is composed of any type of natural vegetation (all growth forms) with a cover from 2 to 10 per cent.
class.description: This class includes any geographical areas were the cover of natural vegetation is between 2 per cent and 10 per cent. This includes permanently or regularly flooded areas.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Terrestrial barren land
class.definition: The category is composed of abiotic natural surfaces.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural abiotic surfaces (bare soil, sand, rocks, etc.) where the natural vegetation is absent or almost absent (covers less than 2 per cent). The class includes areas regularly flooded by inland water (lake shores, river banks, salt flats, etc.). It excludes coastal areas affected by the tidal movement of saltwater (→14).
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Permanent snow and glaciers
class.definition: The category is composed of abiotic natural surfaces.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area covered by snow or glaciers persistently for 10 months or more.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Inland water bodies
class.definition: The category is composed of any type of inland water body with a water persistence of 12 months per year.
class.description: This class includes any geographical area covered for most of the year by inland water bodies. In some cases, the water can be frozen for part of the year (less than 10 months). Because the geographical extent of water bodies can change, boundaries must be set consistently with those set by class 11, according to the dominant situation during the year and/or across multiple years.
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

class.name: Coastal water bodies and intertidal areas
class.definition: The category is composed on the basis of geographical features in relation to the sea (lagoons and estuaries) and abiotic surfaces subject to water persistence (intertidal variations).
class.description: The class is defined on the basis of geographical features of the land in relation to the sea (coastal water bodies, i.e., lagoons and estuaries) and abiotic surfaces subject to water persistence (intertidal areas, i.e., coastal flats and coral reefs).
class.legend_Name: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) land cover legend

name: Corine land cover legend

class.name: Mineral extraction
class.definition: Areas with open-pit extraction of construction material (sand pits, quarries) or other minerals (open-cast mines).Includes flooded gravel pits, except for river-bed extraction.

class.name: Dump site
class.definition: Public, industrial or mine dumpsites.

class.name: Construction sites
class.definition: Spaces under construction development, soil or bed rock excavations, earthworks.

class.name: Urban park
class.definition: Areas with vegetation within urban fabric, includes parks and cemeteries with vegetation, and mansions and their grounds.

class.name: Sport facilities
class.definition: Camping grounds, sports grounds, leisure parks, golf courses, race courses, etc. Includes formal parks not surrounded by urban areas.

class.name: Non irrigated arable land
class.definition: Cereals, legumes, fodder crops, root crops and fallow land. Includes flowers and fruit trees (nurseries cultivation) and vegetables, whether open field, under plastic or glass (includes market gardening). Includes aromatic, medicinal and culinary plants. Does not include permanent pastures.

class.name: Permanently irrigated land
class.definition: Crops irrigated permanently or periodically, using a permanent infrastructure (irrigation channels, drainage network).Most of these crops cannot be cultivated without an artificial water supply. Does not include sporadically irrigated land.

class.name: Rice fields
class.definition: Land prepared for rice cultivation. Flat surfaces with irrigation channels. Surfaces periodically flooded.

class.name: Vineyards
class.definition: Areas planted with vines.

class.name: Fruit trees and berry plantation
class.definition: Parcels planted with fruit trees or shrubs: single or mixed fruit species, fruit trees associated with permanently grassed surfaces. Includes chestnut and walnut groves.

class.name: Olives groves
class.definition: Areas planted with olive trees, including mixed occurrence of olive trees and vines on the same parcel.

class.name: Pasture
class.definition: Dense grass, cover of floral composition, dominated by graminacea, not under a rotation system. Mainly for grazing, but the fodder maybe harvested mechanically. Includes areas with hedges (bocage).

class.name: Annual crops associated with permanent crops
class.definition: Non-permanent crops (arable land or pasture) associated with permanent crops on the same parcel.

class.name: Complex cultivation pattern
class.definition: Juxtaposition of small parcels of diverse annual crops, pasture and/or permanent crops.

class.name: Land principally occupied by agriculture with signficant areas of natural vegetation
class.definition: Areas principally occupied by agriculture, interspersed with significant natural areas.

class.name: Agroforestry areas
class.definition: Annual crops or grazing land under the wooded cover of forestry species.

class.name: Broadleaved forest
class.definition: Vegetation formation composed principally of trees, including shrub and bush under storeys, where broad-leaved species predominate.

class.name: Coniferous forest
class.definition: Vegetation formation composed principally of trees, including shrub and bush under storeys, where coniferous species predominate.

class.name: Mixed forest
class.definition: Vegetation formation composed principally of trees, including shrub and bush under storeys, where neither broad-leaved nor coniferous species predominate.

class.name: Natural grassland
class.definition: Low productivity grassland. Often situated in areas of rough, uneven ground. Frequently includes rocky areas, briars and heathland.

class.name: Moors and heathland
class.definition: Vegetation with low and closed cover, dominated by bushes, shrubs and herbaceous plants (heather, briars, broom, gorse, laburnum, etc.).

class.name: Sclerophillous vegetation
class.definition: Bushy sclerophyllous vegetation, includes maquis and garrigue. In case of shrub vegetation areas composed of sclerophyllous species such as Juniperus oxycedrus and heathland species such as Buxus spp. or Ostrya carpinifolia with no visible dominance (each species occupy about 50% of the area), priority will be given to sclerophyllous vegetation and the whole area will be assigned class 323.

class.name: Transitional woodland-scrub
class.definition: Bushy or herbaceous vegetation with scattered trees. Can represent either woodland degradation or forest regeneration/recolonisation.

class.name: Sparse vegetation
class.definition: Beaches, dunes and expanses of sand or pebbles in coastal or continental locations, including beds of stream channels with torrential regime.

class.name: Bare rocks
class.definition: Scree, clifs, rock outcrops, including active erosion, rocks and reef flats situated above the high-water mark.

class.name: Sparsely vegetated areas
class.definition: Includes steppes, tundra and badlands. Scattered high-altitude vegetation.

class.name: Brunt areas
class.definition: Areas affected by recent fires, still mainly black.

class.name: Glaciers and perennial snow
class.definition: Land covered by glaciers or permanent snowfields

class.name: Inland marches
class.definition: Low-lying land usually flooded in winter, and more or less saturated by water all year round.

class.name: Peat bogs
class.definition: Peatland consisting mainly of decomposed moss and vegetable matter.

class.name: Salt marshes
class.definition: Vegetated low-lying areas, above the high-tide line, susceptible to flooding by sea water. Often, in the process of filling in, gradually being colonized by halophilic plants.

class.name: Salines
class.definition: Salt-pans, active or in process of abandonment. Sections of salt marsh exploited for the production of salt by evaporation. They are clearly distinguishable from the rest of the marsh by their parcellation and embankment systems.

class.name: Intertidal flats
class.definition: Generally unvegetated expanses of mud, sand or rock lying between high and low water marks. 0 m contour on maps.

class.name: Water course
class.definition: Natural or artificial water-courses serving as water drainage channels. Includes canals. Minimum width for inclusion: 100 m.

class.name: Water bodies
class.definition: Natural or artificial stretches of water.

class.name: Coastal lagoons
class.definition: Stretches of salt or brackish water in coastal areas which are separated from the sea by a tongue of land or other similar topography. These water bodies can be connected to the sea at limited points, either permanently or for parts of the year only.

class.name: Estuaries
class.definition: The mouth of a river within which the tide ebbs and flows.

class.name: Sea and ocean
class.definition: Zone seaward of the lowest tide limit.

class.name: Urban dense
class.definition: Most of the land is covered by structures and the transport network. Building, roads and artificially surfaced areas cover more than 80 % of the total surface. Non-linear areas of vegetation and bare soil are exceptional.

class.name: Urban open
class.definition: Most of the land is covered by structures. Building, roads and artificially surfaced areas associated with vegetated areas and bare soil, which occupy discontinuous but significant surfaces.

class.name: Industrial
class.definition: Artificially surfaced areas (with concrete, asphalt, tarmacadam or stabilised, e.g. beaten earth) without vegetation occupy most of the area, which also contains buildings and/or vegetation.

class.name: Road and rail networks and associated areas
class.definition: Motorways and railways, including associated installations (stations, platforms, embankments). Minimum width for inclusion: 100 m.

class.name: Port areas
class.definition: Infrastructure of port areas, including quays, dockyards and marinas.

class.name: Airports
class.definition: Airports installations: runways, buildings and associated land.

name: Anderson land use and land cover classification legend

class.name: Residential (urban or built up)
class.definition: Residential land uses range from high density, represented by the multiple-unit structures of urban cores, to low density, where houses are on lots of more than an acre, on the periphery of urban expansion.

class.name: Commercial and services (urban or built up)
class.definition: Commercial areas are those used predominantly for the sale of products and services. They are often abutted by residential, agricultural, or other contrasting uses which help define them.

class.name: Industrial (urban or built up)
class.definition: Industrial areas include a wide array of land uses from light manufacturing to heavy manufacturing plants. Identification of light industries-those focused on design, assembly, finishing, processing, and packaging of products-can often be based on the type of building, parking, and shipping arrangements.

class.name: Transportation, communication and utilities
class.definition: The land uses included in the Transportation, Communications, and Utilities category occur to some degree within all of the other Urban or Builtup categories and actually can be found within many other categories.

class.name: Industrial and commercial
class.definition: The Industrial and Commercial Complexes category includes those industrial and commercial land uses that typically occur together or in close functional proximity. Such areas commonly are labeled with terminology such as "Industrial Park," but since functions such as warehousing, wholesaling, and occasionally retailing may be found in the same structures or nearby, the more inclusive category title has been adopted.

class.name: Mixed urban or built up land
class.definition: The Mixed Urban or Built-up category is used for a mixture of Level II Urban or Built-up uses where individual uses cannot be separated at mapping scale. Where more than one-third intermixture of another use or uses occurs in a specific area, it is classified as Mixed Urban or Built-up Land. Where the intermixed land use or uses total less than one-third of the specific area, the category appropriate to the dominant land use is applied.

class.name: Other urban or built up land
class.definition: Other Urban or Built-up Land typically consists of uses such as golf driving ranges, zoos, urban parks, cemeteries, waste dumps, water-control structures and spillways, the extensive parts of such uses as golf courses and ski areas, and undeveloped land within an urban setting.

class.name: Cropland and pasture
class.definition: The several components of Cropland and Pasture now used for agricultural statistics include: crop land harvested, including bush fruits; cultivated summer-fallow and idle cropland; land on which crop failure occurs; cropland in soil-improvement grasses and legumes; cropland used only for pasture in rotation with crops; and past~re on land more or less permanently used for that purpose.

class.name: Horchards
class.definition: Orchards, groves, and vineyards produce the various fruit and nut crops. Nurseries and horticultural areas, which include floricultural and seed-and-sod areas and some greenhouses, are used perennially for those purposes.

class.name: Confined feeding operations
class.definition: Confined Feeding Operations are large, specialized livestock production enterprises, chiefly beef cattle feedlots, dairy operations with confined feeding, and large poultry farms, but also including hog feedlots. These operations have large animal populations restricted to relatively small areas.

class.name: Herbaceous rangeland
class.definition: The Herbaceous Rangeland category encompasses lands dominated by naturally occurring grasses and forbs as well as those areas of actual rangeland which have been modified to include grasses and forbs as their principal cover, when the land is managed for rangeland purposes and not managed using practices typical of pastureland.

class.name: Shrub and brush rangeland
class.definition: The typical shrub occurrences are found in those arid and semiarid regions characterized by such xerophytic vegetative types with woody stems as big sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata), shadscale , greasewood (Sarcobatus vermiculatus), or creosote bush (Larrea divaricata) andalso by the typical desert succulent xerophytes, such as the various forms of Cactus.

class.name: Deciduous forest
class.definition: Deciduous Forest Land includes all forested areas having a predominance of trees that lose their leaves at the end of the frost-free season or at the beginning of a dry season.

class.name: Evergreen forest
class.definition: Evergreen Forest Land includes all forested areas in which the trees are predominantly those which remain green throughout the year.

class.name: Mixed forrst
class.definition: Mixed Forest Land includes all forested areas where both evergreen and deciduous trees are growing and neither predominates.

class.name: Streams and canals
class.definition: The Streams and Canals category includes rivers, creeks, canals, and other linear water bodies. Where the water course is interrupted by a control structure, the impounded area will be placed in the Reservoirs category.

class.name: Lakes
class.definition: Lakes are nonflowing, naturally enclosed bodies of water, including regulated natural lakes but excluding reservoirs.

class.name: Reservoir
class.definition: Reservoirs are artificial impoundments of water used for irrigation, flood control, municipal water supplies, recreation, hydroelectric power generation, and so forth.

class.name: Bay and estuaries
class.definition: Bays and Estuaries are inlets or arms of the sea that extend inland.

class.name: Forested wetland
class.definition: Forested Wetlands are wetlands dominated by woody vegetation. Forested Wetland includes season-ally flooded bottomland hardwoods, mangrove swamps, shrub swamps, and wooded swamps ineluding those around bogs.

class.name: Non forested wetlands
class.definition: Non-forested Wetlands are dominated by wetland herbaceous vegetation or are nonvegetated.

class.name: Dry salt flats
class.definition: Dry Salt Flats occurring on the flat-floored bottoms of interior desert basins which do not qualify as Wetland are included in this category.

class.name: Beaches
class.definition: Beaches are the smooth sloping accumulations of sand and gravel along shorelines.

class.name: Sandy areas other than beaches
class.definition: Sandy Areas other than Beaches are composed primarily of dunes -accumulations of sand transported by the wind.

class.name: Bare rock
class.definition: The Bare Exposed Rock category includes areas of bedrock exposure, des,ert pavement, scarps, talus, slides, volcanic material, rock glaciers, and other accumulations of rock without vegetative cover, with the exception of such rock exposures occurring in tundra regions.

class.name: Strip mines, quarries and gravel pits
class.definition: Those extractive mining activities that have significant surface expression are included in this category.

class.name: Shrub and bush tundra
class.definition: The Shrub and Brush Tundra category consists of the various woody shrubs and brushy thickets found in the tundra environment.

class.name: Herbaceouse tundra
class.definition: Herbaceous Tundra is composed of various sedges, grasses, forbs, lichens, and mosses, all of which lack woody stems.

class.name: Bare ground tundra
class.definition: Wet Tundra is usually found in areas having little topographic relief.

class.name: Perennial snowfields
class.definition: The Bare Ground Tundra category is intended for those tundra occurrences which are less than one third of vegetation

class.name: Glaciers
class.definition: Glacial ice originates from the compaction of snow into firn and finally to ice under the weight of several successive annual accumulations.

class.name: Perennial snowfields
class.definition: Perennial Snowfields are accumulations of snow and firn that did not entirely melt during previous summers

class.name: Herbaceous rangeland/shrub and brush rangeland
class.definition: Mixed Rangeland

class.name: Dry salt flats/bare rock/strip mines, quarries and gravel pits
class.definition: The Mixed Barren Land category is used when a mixture of Barren Land features occurs and the dominant land use occupies less than two-thirds of the area.

class.name: Shrub and bush tundra/herbaceouse tundra/wet tundra
class.definition: The Mixed Tundra category is used for a mixture of the Level II Tundra occurrences where any particular type occupies less than two-thirds of the area of the mapping unit.

class.name: Bamboo
class.definition: Area dominated by bamboo.

class.name: Village
class.definition: The patch of land with houses and garden surrounding house.

class.name: Built-up
class.definition: The patch of land with building and construction.

class.name: Deciduous forest
class.definition: Comprised of dry mixed deciduous forest and dry Dipterocarp forests.

class.name: Evergreen forest
class.definition: Areas covered by trees maintaining their leaves during the whole year.

class.name: Flooded forest
class.definition: This forest type is found in Tonle Sap Lake. Most of the forests are low and disturbed. In many cases, there is only a mosaic remaining.

class.name: Forest regrowth

name: Land cover legend for GLC-SHARE

class.name: Artificial Surfaces
class.definition: The class is composed of any type of areas with a predominant artificial surface.Any urban or related feature is included in this class, for example urban parks (parks, parkland, sport facilities). The class also includes industrial areas, waste dump deposit and extraction sites.

class.name: Cropland
class.definition: This class contains three different crop types including Herbaceous Crops, Woody Crops and Multiple or Layered crops. Herbaceous crops is composed of a main layer of cultivated herbaceous plants (graminoids or forbs). It includes herbaceous crops used for hay. All the non-perennial crops that do not last for more than two growing seasons and crops like sugar cane where the upper part of the plant is regularly harvested while the root system can remain for more than one year in the field are included in this class. Woody Crops is composed of a main layer of permanent crops (trees and/or shrub crops) and includes all types of orchards and plantations (fruit trees, coffee and tea plantation, oil palms, rubber plantation, Christmas trees etc.). Multiple or Layered crops combine different land cover situations: - Two layers of different crops (woody + herbaceous): A common case is the presence of one layer of woody crops (trees or shrubs) and another layer of herbaceous crop, such as for wheat fields with olive trees in the Mediterranean area and intense horticulture, oasis or typical coastal African agriculture were herbaceous fields are covered by palm trees, etc. - Presence of one important layer of natural vegetation (mainly trees) that cover one layer of cultivated crops: A typical example are coffee plantations shadowed by natural trees in the equatorial area of Africa.

class.name: Grassland
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural herbaceous plants (grasslands, prairies, steppes and savannahs) with a cover of 10% or more, irrespective of different human and/or animal activities, such as: grazing, selective fire management etc. Woody plants (trees and/or shrubs) can be present assuming their cover is less that 10%.

class.name: Tree Covered Area
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural tree plants with a cover of 10% or more. Other types of plants (shrubs and/or herbs) can be present, even with a density higher than trees. Areas planted with trees for afforestation purposes and forest plantations are included in this class. This class includes areas seasonally or permanently flooded with fresh water. It excludes coastal mangroves (→07).

class.name: Shrubs Covered Area
class.definition: This class includes any geographical area dominated by natural shrubs having a cover of 10% or more. Trees can be present in scattered form if their cover is less than 10%. Herbaceous plants can also be present at any density. The class includes shrub covered areas permanently or regularly flooded by inland fresh water. It excludes shrubs flooded by salt or brackish water in coastal areas (→07).

class.name: Herbaceous vegetation, aquatic or regularly flooded
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural herbaceous vegetation (cover of 10% or more) that is permanently or regularly flooded by fresh or brackish water (swamps, marsh areas etc.). Flooding must persist for at least 2 months per year to be considered regular. Woody vegetation (trees and/or shrubs) can be present if their cover is less than 10%.

class.name: Mangroves
class.definition: This class includes any geographical area dominated by woody vegetation (trees and/or shrubs) with a cover of 10% or more that is permanently or regularly flooded by salt and/or brackish water located in the coastal areas or in the deltas of rivers.

class.name: Sparse vegetation
class.definition: This class includes any geographic areas were the cover of natural vegetation is between 2% and 10%. This includes permanently or regularly flooded areas.

class.name: BareSoil
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural abiotic surfaces (bare soil, sand, rocks, etc.) where the natural vegetation is absent or almost absent (covers less than 2%). The class includes areas regularly flooded by inland water (lake shores, river banks, salt flats etc.). It excludes coastal areas affected by the tidal movement of salt water.

class.name: Snow and glaciers
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area covered by snow or glaciers persistently for 10 months or more.

class.name: Waterbodies
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area covered for most of the year by inland water bodies. In some cases the water can be frozen for part of the year (less than 10 months). Because the geographic extent of water bodies can change, boundaries must be set consistently with class 11 according to the dominant situation during the year and/or across multiple years.

name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Infrastructure
class.definition: This land is characterized by the presence of buildings, roads and artificial surfaces. Different types of builtup areas can be included in this classs, such as urban areas, airports and oil fields.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Forest
class.definition: This land is characterized by the presence of dense natural forests, bushes and shrubs are also common in these areas.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Cultivated land
class.definition: This land consists of agricultural fields which may feature various types of crops such as wheat and barley, horticultural crops (e.g. tomatoes and potatoes), legumes and forage crops. The crop water management in these areas may be irrigated or rainfed.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Bare soil
class.definition: This land consists of bare soil which is not used for cultivation and usually devoid of grass and shrub cover.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Spare vegetation
class.definition: This land is categorized by bare soil which is sparsely populated with shrubs and grasses. This land is unmanaged and is not used for cultivation or grazing purposes.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Meadow
class.definition: This land consists of relatively dense herbaceous natural vegetation, occasionally populated by sparse shrubs and trees.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Sugarcane
class.definition: This class consists of agricultural land which is used for the cultivation of sugarcane.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Mangrove
class.definition: This class consists of intertidal forest land. It is characterized by the presence of trees and water bodies.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Water
class.definition: This land is characterized by the presence of water bodies, including both natural and artificial non - perennial freshwater bodies (flowing and stagnant).
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Wetland
class.definition: This class consists of swamp and wetland areas in which herbaceous or aquaic vegetation are present. It may include pemanent or semi permanent wetland.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Grassland
class.definition: This class is categorized by the prevalence of herbaceous vegetation, mainly grasses, with sparse trees or shurbs occasionally being present.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Orchard
class.definition: This land consists of orchards cultivated for the production of fruits (i.e. organge, citrus, fig, apple, peach and apricot) or other types of plantations.
class.legend_Name: Sub-national land cover legend for Mozambique

class.name: Rainfed orchards
class.definition: The land is covered by rainfed orchards cultivated for the production of fruits (i.e., orange, citrus, fig, apple, peach and apricot), and other type of plantations

class.name: Irrigated orchards
class.definition: The land is covered by irrigated orchards cultivated for the production of fruits (i.e., orange, citrus, fig, apple, peach and apricot), and other type of plantations

class.name: Bare soIl
class.definition: The land is covered by bare area/undifferentiated area not used for cultivation and usuallydevoid of grass and shrub cover (i.e. bare soil areas are characterized by NDVI (values close to zero).

class.name: Forest
class.definition: The land is primarily covered by desnse natural forests with the presence of bushes and shrubs also possible.

class.name: Infrastructure
class.definition: The land is covered by infrastructure as buildings, roads and artifiical surfaced areas. Different types of buildup are included in this class (i.e. urban, airports, oilfields).

class.name: Marquis/garrigue
class.definition: The land is covered by relatively dense shrubs, ocassionally interspersed with sparse trees and herbaceous vegetation.

class.name: Rainfed olives
class.definition: The land is covered by rainfed olive orchards. These cultivated groves are characterized by the sparse clustering of olive trees, forming a pattern that provides a distinctive appearance to an orchard setting with presence of bare soil.

class.name: Irrigated olives
class.definition: The land is covered by irrigated olive orchards. These cultivated groves are characterized by the sparse clustering of olive trees, forming a pattern that provides a distintive appearance to an orchard setting with presence of bare soil.

class.name: Other rainfed crop
class.definition: The land is covered by rainfed agricultural fields, featuring various types of crops: cereal crops such as wheat and barley, horticultural crops like tomatoes and melonds, legumes, and forage crops. The crop water management in these areas is rainfed.

class.name: Other irrigated crop
class.definition: The land is covered by irrigated agricultural fields, featuring various types of crops: cereal crops such as wheat and barley, horticultural crops like tomatoes and melonds, legumes, and forage crops. The crop water management in these areas is irrigated.

class.name: Irrigated dates
class.definition: The land is covered by irrigated date. The presence of date tress dominates the land cover (about 80 %). In some cases pomegranate trees and forage crops may be present to benefit from oasis irrigation.

class.name: Water and wetlands
class.definition: The land is covered by water areas. Within this land cover class are included natural and artificial non - perennial freshwater body (flowing and standing).

name: National land cover legend for Burkina Faso

class.name: Open forest
class.definition: Tree formation characterized by large trees (15 to 20m high), with more or less contiguous crowns with a shrub layer which constitutes a light undergrowth. The recovery rate is between 50 and 70% with a sparse distribution. It is marked by the presence of grasses and a grassy layer.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Formation arborée caractérisée par des arbres de grande taille (15 à 20m de haut), aux cimes plus ou moins jointives avec une strate arbustive qui constitue un sous-bois clair. Le taux de recouvrement est compris entre 50 et 70 % avec une répartition clairsemée. Elle est marquée par la présence de graminées et d’une strate herbeuse.

class.name: Gallery forest
class.definition: Linear in shape, this plant formation runs along watercourses and appears as a riparian barrier and is made up of tree species or deciduous forest. It is sometimes destroyed in places for the benefit of agricultural developments. It is easily identifiable in the image by its shape and tone which generally contrasts with the immediate environment when the latter has been degraded by man.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: De forme linéaire, cette formation végétale longe les cours d’eau et se présente sous l’aspect de cordon ripicole et est fait d’espèces arborées ou de forêt décidue. Elle est parfois détruite par endroits au profit des aménagements agricoles. Elle est facilement identifiable sur l’image par sa forme et le ton qui tranche généralement avec l’environnement immédiat lorsque ce dernier a été dégradé par l’homme.

class.name: Forest plantation
class.definition: This type of occupation refers to any form of vegetation made of trees planted by man for various needs (wood production, restoration and protection of soil). Generally isolated in highly humanized spaces, it appears on the image as a spot with sometimes a geometric shape. However, confusion is possible with sacred groves or other natural formations.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Ce type d’occupation désigne toute forme de végétation faite d’arbres plantés par l’homme pour des besoins divers (productions de bois, restauration et protection des sols). Généralement isolé dans des espaces fortement humanisés, il apparait sur l’image sous l’aspect d’une tache avec parfois une forme géométrique. Cependant, des confusions sont possibles avec les bois sacrés ou autres formations naturelles.

class.name: Tree savannah
class.definition: This formation is present in the Sudanian phytogeographic domain. It is a grouping of trees mixed with a grassy layer and shrubs. The tree coverage rate is greater than 10% but less than 50%. The tree layer has a height that varies between 10 and 20 m, with well-individualized trees scattered within the shrub layer.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Cette formation est présente dans le domaine phytogéographique soudanien. Il s’agit d’un regroupement d’arbres auquel se mêle une strate herbeuse et des arbustes. Le taux de recouvrement des arbres est supérieur à 10 % mais inférieur à 50 %. La strate arborescente a une hauteur qui varie entre 10 et 20 m, avec des arbres bien individualisés et disséminés à l’intérieur de la strate arbustive.

class.name: Tree steppe
class.definition: This plant formation is especially present in the northern parts of Burkina Faso (sub-Sahelian phytogeographic sector) and strongly represented for example in the regions of Tougri-Yalgo, Djibo-Kongoussi. It presents itself in the form of an alternation of tree strata (7 to 12 m) and bare soils of small extent (compared to the vegetation), sometimes occupied by a rare herbaceous carpet dotted with termite mounds.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Cette formation végétale est surtout présente dans les parties septentrionales du Burkina Faso (secteur phytogéographique subsahélien) et fortement représentée par exemple dans les régions de Tougri-Yalgo, Djibo-Kongoussi. Elle se présente sous forme d’une alternance de strates arborées (7 à 12 m) et de sols nus de faibles étendues (comparés à la végétation), parfois occupées par un tapis herbacé rare parsemé de termitières.

class.name: Agroforestry park
class.definition: These are the plant formations which mainly occupy the crop fields. They result from selective deforestation when the field was opened. This plant formation can also occupy plots left fallow. Their recovery rate must be greater than 25% of the entire territory. The trees must be composed mainly of forest species. Their identification on the image essentially takes into account the agricultural territories, in particular the particular characteristics of the tree layer found there. This formation has a variable appearance depending on the rate of coverage, the nature of the species on which the shape of the crowns, the foliage and the vegetative cycle depend.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Ce sont les formations végétales qui occupent principalement les champs de cultures. Elles résultent d’un déboisement sélectif lors de l’ouverture du champ. Cette formation végétale peut occuper aussi les parcelles laissées en jachère. Leur taux de recouvrement doit être supérieur à 25 % de l’ensemble du territoire. Les arbres doivent être composés en majorité d’espèces forestières. Leur identification sur l’image tient essentiellement compte des territoires agricoles, notamment des caractéristiques particulières de la strate arborée qui s’y trouve. Cette formation a une apparence variable en fonction du taux de recouvrement, de la nature des espèces dont dépend la forme des houppiers, le feuillage et le cycle végétatif.

class.name: Shrub savannah
class.definition: This type of savannah is characterized by the dominance of shrub species with a coverage of between 10 and 50%. The shrubs are between 4 and 7 m high and are overlooked by a few rare trees scattered here and there, whose coverage is less than 10%. A high herbaceous stratum (1 to 1.5 m) and a lower stratum also occupy this plant formation. Its recognition in images is not always easy because of the physiognomic variability created according to the climatic seasons and which has an effect on reflectance.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Ce type de savane est caractérisé par la dominance des espèces arbustives avec un recouvrement compris entre 10 et 50 %. Les arbustes ont une taille entre 4 et 7 m de haut et sont surplombés par quelques rares arbres disséminés çà et là, dont le recouvrement est inférieur à 10 %. Une strate herbacée haute (1 à 1,5 m) et une strate inférieure occupent aussi cette formation végétale. Sa reconnaissance sur les images n’est pas toujours aisée à cause de la variabilité physionomique créée en fonction des saisons climatiques et qui a un effet sur la réflectance.

class.name: Shrub steppe
class.definition: This unit has the same structure as the tree steppe, marked by the alternation of vegetation and bare soil. However, in the present case, the vegetation consists of the shrub layer (4 to 6 m).
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Cette unité présente la même structure que la steppe arborée, marquée par l’alternance de végétation et de sol nu. Cependant, dans le cas présent, la végétation est constituée par la strate arbustive (4 à 6 m).

class.name: Housing
class.definition: It is all the infrastructures that house the different human groups. The perception of the habitat in an image is linked to its structure and the nature of the materials used. Housing in urban areas is in the form of a continuous or discontinuous fabric depending on the size of the population and the density of the habitat. This type of housing is made up of well-structured buildings and well-marked roads. This structure is easily perceptible in the image by its blue or other color depending on the colored composition, as well as the geometric shapes of the habitat and the roads. In the case of continuous urban fabric, vegetation is very little present and the coverage of artificial surfaces reaches more than 80% in these places. These types of surfaces are present in the towns of regional and provincial capitals and in the state capital. However, in the case of discontinuous urban fabric, the structure of the habitat is an alternation of artificialized spaces and vegetation. In this case, the artificialized surfaces have a coverage of more than 30% but less than 80%. This structure characterizes the outskirts of the capital, regional and provincial capitals. They also characterize the capitals of departments as well as urban areas in rural areas. As for housing in rural areas, it is dominated by unstructured groupings of buildings. The coverage of artificialized surfaces is less than 30%. This type of habitat is quite diffuse among crops and vegetation so that it is not identifiable in the images. The use of other sources and documents (topographic sheet, database, very high resolution image) is necessary to supplement the information.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: C’est l’ensemble des infrastructures qui abritent les différents regroupements humains. La perception de l’habitat sur une image est liée à sa structure et à la nature des matériaux utilisés. L’habitat en milieu urbain se présente sous forme d’un tissu continu ou discontinu en fonction de l’importance du peuplement et de la densité de l’habitat. Ce type d’habitat est composé de bâtiments bien structurés et d’une voirie bien tracée. Cette structure est facilement perceptible sur l’image par sa couleur bleue ou autre en fonction de la composition colorée, ainsi que les formes géométriques de l’habitat et de la voirie. Dans le cas du tissu urbain continu, la végétation est très peu présente et le recouvrement des surfaces artificialisées atteint en ces lieux plus de 80 %. Ces types de surfaces sont présents dans les agglomérations des chefs lieu de région et de province et dans la capitale de l’Etat. Cependant, dans le cas du tissu urbain discontinu, la structure de l’habitat est une alternance d’espaces artificialisées et de végétation. Dans ce cas, les surfaces artificialisées ont un recouvrement de plus de 30 % mais inférieure à 80 %. Cette structure caractérise la périphérie de la capitale, des chefs lieu de région et de provinces. Elles caractérisent également les chefs lieu de département aussi les agglomérations des zones rurales.

class.name: Annual cultivation
class.definition: These are crops grown regularly each year and dependent on the rainfall regime. They are made up of cereal crops (millet, corn, sorghum, cotton, etc.), fodder crops, those produced for food seasoning and medical needs, as well as oilseeds and certain vegetable crops such as okra. The plant cover in these units is less than 25% and they are recognizable in the images by the structure of the plot and the plant cover combined with the nature of the soil, in particular the types of materials in place. There are also irrigated crops: these types of crops are grown using appropriate arrangements allowing the supply of water by gravity, by sprinkling or by dripping. This is linked to the fact that these crops are grown in the dry season, which is why their identification on the image is done using scenes taken on the dates of production of these crops. These crops are easily identifiable in the images by their geometric shapes, the presence of developments and the contrast they cause in the dry season. They are practiced alternating with rainfed crops. The main products are: tomatoes, onions, cabbages, green beans, potatoes, rice etc.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Il s’agit des cultures pratiquées régulièrement chaque année et tributaires du régime pluviométrique. Elles sont composées de cultures céréalières (mil, mais, sorgho, coton, etc.), fourragères, celles produites pour l’assaisonnement des aliments et les besoins de la médecine, ainsi que les oléagineux et certaines cultures légumières telles que le gombo. Le recouvrement végétal dans ces unités est inférieur à 25 % et elles sont reconnaissables sur les images par la structure du parcellaire et le recouvrement végétal combiné avec la nature du sol, notamment les types de matériaux en place. Il y a aussi les cultures irriguées : ces types de cultures sont pratiqués à l’aide d’aménagements appropriés permettant l’approvisionnement en eau par gravité, par aspersion ou par gouttes. Cela est lié au fait que ces cultures sont pratiquées en saison sèche, raison pour laquelle leur identification sur l’image se fait à l’aide des scènes prises aux dates de production de ces cultures. Ces cultures sont facilement identifiables sur les images de par leurs formes géométriques, la présence des aménagements et le contraste qu’elles provoquent en saison sèche. Elles sont pratiquées en alternance avec les cultures pluviales. Les principaux produits sont : tomate, oignon, choux, haricot vert, pomme de terre, riz etc.

class.name: Rice field
class.definition: This is rice production. This cereal production can be classified into both rainfed and irrigated crops. Depending on the type of variety, rice can be grown in the rainy season using rainwater, or in the dry season. In the second case, production takes place in the shallows. It is traditionally practiced in lowlands without development but is also practiced in lowlands equipped with hydro-agricultural development allowing the supply of water for production outside the rainy season. The latter case is easily identifiable in the images. On the other hand, rainfed rice blends in with other crops, making its identification more difficult.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Il s’agit de la production du riz. Cette production céréalière peut être classée aussi bien dans les cultures pluviales et irriguées. En fonction du type de variété, le riz peut être cultivé en saison pluvieuse en utilisant l’eau de la pluie, ou en saison sèche. Dans le second cas, la production se fait dans les basfonds. Elle est pratiquée traditionnellement dans des basfonds sans aménagement mais est aussi pratiquée dans des basfonds équipées d’un aménagement hydroagricole permettant l’approvisionnement en eau pour la production hors saison pluvieuse. Ce dernier cas est facilement identifiable sur les images. En revanche, le riz pluvial se confond aux autres productions rendant son identification plus difficile.

class.name: Permanent culture
class.definition:
These are crops that are grown all year round without interruption. Industrial crops and orchards are grouped together in this unit. Industrial crops in the case of Burkina Faso boil down to sugar cane, for example, cultivated over vast areas with sophisticated technical means for sprinkler irrigation. It is easily identifiable in the images by the shape of the plots and the extent of the crops.
There are also orchards which consist of plantations of fruit trees intended mainly for food products. These include, for example, mango orchards, cashew trees, guava trees, etc. their extent varies but they are difficult to identify from Landsat images. However, enormous field work supplemented by documentation makes it possible to recognize them.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA:
Ce sont des cultures qui sont pratiquées toute l’année sans interruption. Sont regroupés dans cette unité les cultures industrielles et les vergers. Les cultures industrielles dans le cas du Burkina Faso se résument à celle de la canne à sucre par exemple, exploitée sur de vastes superficies avec des moyens techniques perfectionnés pour l’irrigation par aspersion. Elle est facilement identifiable sur les images par la forme des parcelles et l’étendue des cultures.
Il y a aussi les vergers qui sont constitués de plantations d’arbres fruitiers destinés essentiellement aux produits alimentaires. Il s’agit par exemple des vergers de manguiers, d’anacardiers, de goyaviers etc. leur étendue est variable mais ils sont difficilement identifiables à partir des images landsat. Un énorme travail de terrain complété par la documentation permet cependant de les reconnaitre.

class.name: Orchard
class.definition: These are plots planted with fruit trees; pure crops or mixture of fruit species, fruit trees in association with areas always covered with grass. Satellite images are only suitable for recognizing orchards and fruit plantations based on their geometric shape printed by man if they are large. The use of exogenous data (aerial photographs, topographical maps) and field campaigns are essential for their recognition. Citrus fruits, mango trees, papayas, banana trees, cashews etc. are included in this class.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Ce sont des parcelles plantées d’arbres fruitiers ; cultures pures ou mélange d’espèces fruitières, arbres fruitiers en association avec des surfaces toujours en herbes. Les images satellites ne se prêtent à la reconnaissance des vergers et des plantations fruitières qu’à leur forme géométrique imprimée par l’homme si elles sont d’envergure. L’utilisation de données exogènes (photographies aériennes, cartes topographiques) et les campagnes sur le terrain sont indispensables pour leur reconnaissance. Les agrumes, manguiers, papayes, bananiers, anacardes etc. sont inclus dans cette classe.

class.name: Wetland
class.definition: These are low-lying lands generally flooded during the rainy season. Sparsely forested areas, partially, temporarily or permanently saturated with stagnant or running water.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Ce sont des terres basses généralement inondées pendant la saison des pluies. Zones faiblement boisées, partiellement, temporairement ou permanemment saturées d’eau stagnante ou courante.

class.name: Water surface
class.definition: They represent the courses followed by the continuous natural flow of water on the surface of the ground and draining a given sector. Included in this class are natural and artificial watercourses that serve as water flow channels, including canals. Width to take into account: 100 m. Lakes, ponds, natural ponds and dam reservoirs are included in this class.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Elles représentent les cours suivis par l’écoulement naturel continu de l’eau à la surface du sol et drainant un secteur donné. Sont inclus dans cette classe les cours d’eau naturels et artificiels qui servent de chenal d’écoulement des eaux, y compris les canaux. Largeur à prendre en compte : 100 m. Les lacs, les mares, les étangs naturels, les retenues de barrages sont inclues dans cette classe. Elles se reconnaissent sur les images par leur couleur bleue mais rouge aux endroits où elles sont couvertes de végétations (nénuphars) en surface.

class.name: Grassy Savanna
class.definition: They are areas where trees and shrubs are usually absent (coverage less than 10%). Grassy formations include a continuous grass layer at least 80 cm high.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Elles sont des zones où les arbres et arbustes sont ordinairement absents (recouvrement inférieur à 10 %). Les formations herbeuses comportent une strate graminéenne continue d’au moins 80 cm de hauteur.

class.name: Grassy steppe
class.definition: Sparse grassy formation without trees or shrubs. It is dominated by the annual grass carpet.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Formation herbeuse clairsemée sans arbres ni arbustes. Elle est dominée par le tapis graminéen, annuel.

class.name: Bare soil (eroded, denuded)
class.definition: Soils stripped of plant cover. Generally these soils are loose materials sensitive to erosion (stripping, ablation).
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Sols dégarnis de couvert végétal. Généralement ces sols sont des matériaux meubles sensibles à l’érosion (décapage, ablation). Pas de difficulté majeure (sur les images) pour caractériser ce type d’occupation des terres dont la réflectance particulièrement blanche indique un sol avec une couverture végétale quasiment absente.

class.name: Crusty soil
class.definition: Highly consolidated surface formation resulting from the accumulation of sesquioxides of iron, alumina, or even manganese, common in the tropical zone, where it restricts the agricultural domain. In general, these soils are devoid of plant cover. The grass layer is dominant.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Formation superficielle fortement consolidée résultant de l'accumulation de sesquioxydes de fer, d'alumine, voire de manganèse, fréquente dans la zone tropicale, dont elle restreint le domaine agricole. En général, ces sols sont dégarnis de couvert végétal. La strate graminéenne est dominante.

class.name: Sand dune
class.definition: The dunes are a set of ergs characteristic of the Sahelian regions (with 600 mm of rain per year). The vegetation present must be less than 10%.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Les dunes sont un ensemble d’ergs caractéristiques des régions sahéliennes (de 600 mm de pluie par an). La végétation présente doit être inférieure à 10 %.

class.name: Bare rock
class.definition: Screes, cliffs, rocks, rocky outcrops, lavas, are the main components of this class.
class.legend_Name: Land cover legend for Burkina Faso
class.Definition_FRA: Eboulis, falaise, rochers, affleurements rocheux, les laves, sont les principales composantes de cette classe. Pour l’interprétation de ce poste il est intéressant de consulter la carte topographique et photographies aériennes où elles peuvent s’identifier plus facilement. Ces documents permettent, en outre, de repérer les zones rocheuses dissimulées par les effets d’ombre portée dans les vallées encaissées.

class.name: Tree Cover
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by trees with a cover of 10% or more. Other land cover classes (shrubs and/or herbs in the understorey, built-up, permanent water bodies, …) can be present below the canopy, even with a density higher than trees. Areas planted with trees for afforestation purposes and plantations (e.g. oil palm, olive trees) are included in this class. This class also includes tree covered areas seasonally or permanently flooded with fresh water except for mangroves.

class.name: Shrubland
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural shrubs having a cover of 10% or more. Shrubs are defined as woody perennial plants with persistent and woody stems and without any defined main stem being less than 5 m tall. Trees can be present in scattered form if their cover is less than 10%. Herbaceous plants can also be present at any density. The shrub foliage can be either evergreen or deciduous.

class.name: Grassland
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area dominated by natural herbaceous plants (Plants without persistent stem or shoots above ground and lacking definite firm structure): (grasslands, prairies, steppes, savannahs, pastures) with a cover of 10% or more, irrespective of different human and/or animal activities, such as: grazing, selective fire management etc. Woody plants (trees and/or shrubs) can be present assuming their cover is less than 10%. It may also contain uncultivated cropland areas (without harvest/ bare soil period) in the reference year

class.name: Cropland
class.definition: Land covered with annual cropland that is sowed/planted and harvestable at least once within the 12 months after the sowing/planting date. The annual cropland produces an herbaceous cover and is sometimes combined with some tree or woody vegetation. Note that perennial woody crops will be classified as the appropriate tree cover or shrub land cover type. Greenhouses are considered as built-up.

class.name: Built-up
class.definition: Land covered by buildings, roads and other man-made structures such as railroads. Buildings include both residential and industrial building. Urban green (parks, sport facilities) is not included in this class. Waste dump deposits and extraction sites are considered as bare.

class.name: Bare / sparse vegetation
class.definition: Lands with exposed soil, sand, or rocks and never has more than 10 % vegetated cover during any time of the year

class.name: Snow and Ice
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area covered by snow or glaciers persistently

class.name: Permanent water bodies
class.definition: This class includes any geographic area covered for most of the year (more than 9 months) by water bodies: lakes, reservoirs, and rivers. Can be either fresh or salt-water bodies. In some cases the water can be frozen for part of the year (less than 9 months).

class.name: Herbaceous wetland
class.definition: Land dominated by natural herbaceous vegetation (cover of 10% or more) that is permanently or regularly flooded by fresh, brackish or salt water. It excludes unvegetated sediment (see 60), swamp forests (classified as tree cover) and mangroves see 95)

class.name: Mangroves
class.definition: Taxonomically diverse, salt-tolerant tree and other plant species which thrive in intertidal zones of sheltered tropical shores, "overwash" islands, and estuaries.

class.name: Moss and lichen
class.definition: Land covered with lichens and/or mosses. Lichens are composite organisms formed from the symbiotic association of fungi and algae. Mosses contain photo-autotrophic land plants without true leaves, stems, roots but with leaf-and stemlike organs.

class.definition: Artificial land includes urbanized areas, activity zones, non-built artificial areas, and non-agricultural artificial green spaces.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Olive plantation
class.definition: Olive groves consist of dense olive plantations and less dense cultivation on arable land. In some cases, field visits are necessary for more accurate identification. On satellite images, they appear as dark green patches with brown dots in the center.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Grape field
class.definition: Grape fields are clearly identifiable in aerial photographs, topographic maps, and agricultural statistics. Abandoned grape fields that retain their alignment are also included in this category.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Bare land
class.definition: Bare land without or with scattered vegetation consists of arid lands. This category is divided into bare rock, bare soil, beaches, sand dunes, and islands.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Cereals
class.definition: A cereal refers to any grass plant grown for its edible grains (seeds), which are a staple food source. Cereals grow in Akkar, North Lebanon, and other areas. The term also applies to the grains themselves, which are rich in carbohydrates. Usually, cereals in Lebanon consists of wheat, barley, and corn.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Field crops
class.definition: Field crops include plowed land cultivated with annual, biennial, and triennial herbaceous crops. This category is subdivided into: (1) large open field crops, (2) small open field crops or terraces, (3) abandoned agricultural land, and (4) urban sprawl on open field crops.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Citrus orchard
class.definition: Citrus includes all types of lemons, oranges, clementines, etc., typically found near the coast.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Fruit trees orchard
class.definition: Fruit trees include deciduous or evergreen trees, irrigated or rain-fed, as well as shrubs that produce either stone or pome fruits, along with exotic fruits such as avocados and mangoes. Satellite images are used to identify these orchards. Nurseries and planted pastures are not included in this category.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Greenhouse
class.definition: Crops under cover are crops under greenhouses, in protected area of agriculture.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Cattle raising
class.definition: Cattle raising refers to the place for raising domesticated animals, such as cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and other animals, for agricultural purposes. This includes the production of meat, milk, wool, leather, and other by-products.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Poultry breeding
class.definition: Poultry breeding is the place for raising domesticated birds, such as chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese, primarily for the purpose of producing meat, eggs, or feathers
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Banana orchard
class.definition: Banana trees are located in coastal areas, especially in the South of the Lebanon.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon

class.name: Agriculture equipment
class.definition: Agricultural equipment refers to the storage containing machinery, tools, and implements used in farming and agricultural practices to enhance efficiency, productivity, and ease of operation.
class.legend_Name: National land cover legend for Lebanon
